hypotheses.title: Folding a chain of string-literal `+` is O(N^2) in time and memory, and consts fold it twice (stage 4 and constant evaluator)
hypotheses.issue: A left-nested chain `"a" + "b" + ... ` (N terms) is folded node by node. At every `+` node with two string-singleton operands, semantics/internal/types/type_resolver.go:additiveSingletonType computes `lhs + rhs` (a fresh Go string copy of the whole prefix) and wraps it in semtypes.StringConst, storing it as that node's type; so all N prefixes of the final string (~N^2/2 x term length bytes) are materialised and kept alive by the AST for the whole compilation. This runs in stage 4 for consts and stage 5 for locals. For a `const`, semantics/internal/types/constant_evaluator.go:constantAdd independently builds all the prefixes a second time. In addition semtypes/string_subtype.go:StringConst calls codePointCount (len([]rune(s))) over the full string just to test whether it is a single code point, an extra O(len) scan+allocation per prefix (~12-18% CPU). At N=8000 (304 KB source), additiveSingletonType allocates ~892 MB and constantAdd ~435 MB of 1.39 GB total; stage 4 takes 749 ms and stage 5 310 ms while parse/AST build take ~33 ms each. Doubling N multiplies stage 4/5 time ~3.5-4x and RSS ~3.3x.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a Ballerina file with long chains of string-literal concatenation.

Usage: gen_strconcat.py N > strconcat_N.bal

- A module-level `const string` initialised with N `+`-joined string literals
  (stage 4: resolveAdditiveExpr->additiveSingletonType AND
  constantExpressionEvaluator->constantAdd both fold every prefix).
- A local `string` variable initialised with the same N-term chain inside a
  function that is never called (stage 5: additiveSingletonType folds every
  prefix), so the interpreter never evaluates it.
"""
import sys

n = int(sys.argv[1])
terms = " + ".join(f'"segment-{i:06d}"' for i in range(n))  # 16 chars each
print("import ballerina/io;")
print()
print(f"const string LONG = {terms};")
print()
print("function buildLocal() returns string {")
print(f"    string s = {terms};")
print("    return s;")
print("}")
print()
print("public function main() {")
print("    io:println(LONG.length());")
print("}")
reproducer.command: go build -o /tmp/bal ./cli/cmd && python3 gen_strconcat.py 8000 (writes strconcat_8000.bal) && /usr/bin/time -f 'wall=%es rss=%MKB' /tmp/bal run strconcat_8000.bal ; or ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> strconcat_8000.bal

hypotheses.baseline: main 7844a7b1, N=8000: wall 1.19-1.31 s, max RSS ~1.06 GB; stage 4 (top-level type resolution) 749 ms, stage 5 (local type resolution) 310 ms, parse 32 ms, AST build 34 ms. N=4000: wall 0.44 s, RSS 329 MB. N=16000: wall 4.5 s, RSS 3.85 GB, stage 4 2836 ms, stage 5 1389 ms.

improvement.summary: Reproducer (N=8000) wall time -80.7% (1185 -> 228 ms), peak memory -83% (1053 -> 177 MiB); stage 4 749 -> 42 ms, stage 5 310 -> 46 ms; N=16000 4.5 s/3.85 GB -> 0.48 s/363 MB (now linear). Memory benchmark flagged 'unreliable' (CV ~8%) but at 48 sigma.

hypotheses.fix_approach: Added a tiny per-resolver stringConcatenator (a strings.Builder): concat(lhs, rhs) appends rhs in place when lhs is the string it returned last time, otherwise resets and copies lhs first. Because a strings.Builder never rewrites bytes already written, previously returned strings stay valid, so every intermediate node keeps exactly the same string-singleton type (no golden output changes) but intermediate strings are views into shared buffers; total work becomes linear in the final length. One concatenator per packageTypeResolver and per functionTypeResolver (loop resolvers use their parent's, mirroring resolverXMLStepCounters), so concurrently resolved function bodies never share one; the constant evaluator gets its own concatenator threaded through constantArithmetic/constantAdd. StringConst's single-code-point check became an O(1) utf8.DecodeRuneInString size == len(s) test. Pitfalls: intermediate node types are observable (goldens), so they must not be dropped; the string-equality check on lhs relies on Go's pointer fast path for identical strings. A cleaner from-scratch fix could instead fold the whole chain once (collect leaves) or have the type resolver reuse the constant evaluator's folded value so consts are not folded twice. make test and make test-race pass.

notes: Side findings from exploration, not pursued: (1) parser error recovery blows up on the invalid statement `{f0: var a0, ..., fN: var aN} = r;` (29 s to parse at N=50, 64 s at N=100) - likely worth its own investigation; (2) XML namespace lookup (semantics/internal/symbols/xmlns_resolver.go:lookupXMLNS/localPrefixSpace) walks every ancestor scope per element, quadratic in nesting depth (82 ms at depth 4000, 724 ms at 8000).
